sentences.zh: 孝友者，人之至行也，而恆性存焉。

translations.literal: Filial piety and fraternity are humanity's utmost conduct, and constant nature dwells therein.
translations.idiomatic: Filial devotion and brotherly regard are the highest virtues a person can practice, and they spring from our enduring human nature.

sentences.zh: 有子者欲其孝，有弟者欲其友，豈非人之恆情乎？

translations.literal: Those who have sons wish them to be filial; those who have younger brothers wish them to be friendly — is this not people's constant sentiment?
translations.idiomatic: Parents want their sons to be dutiful, and elder brothers want their juniors to be affectionate — is this not the enduring sentiment of humankind?

sentences.zh: 為子而孝，為弟而友，又豈非人之恆性乎？

translations.literal: To be filial as a son and friendly as a younger brother — is this not also people's constant nature?
translations.idiomatic: To fulfill one's duty as a filial son and an affectionate younger brother — is this not likewise our constant nature?

sentences.zh: 以人之恆情責人之恆性，而不副所欲者恆有焉。

translations.literal: Using people's constant sentiment to demand people's constant nature, those who fail to meet what is desired are ever present.
translations.idiomatic: When we hold people to their innate virtues by the standards of what we always wish for them, there will always be those who fall short of our hopes.

sentences.zh: 有竭力於是，豈非難乎。

translations.literal: To exert all one's strength in this — is it not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: To devote one's utmost effort to this — is that not arduous?

sentences.zh: 天生五穀以養人，五穀之有恆性也。

translations.literal: Heaven produced the five grains to nourish people; the five grains have their constant nature.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven created the five grains to sustain humankind, and the grains themselves possess a fixed nature.

sentences.zh: 服田力穡以望有秋，農夫之有恆情也。

translations.literal: Tilling the fields and laboring at harvest in hope of an autumn crop — this is the farmer's constant sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Working the land and striving at cultivation in expectation of the autumn harvest — this is the farmer's enduring hope.

sentences.zh: 五穀熟，人民育，豈異事乎。

translations.literal: When the five grains ripen, the people are nourished — are these not the same affair?
translations.idiomatic: When the grains ripen and the people thrive, are these not one and the same outcome?

sentences.zh: 然以唐、虞之世，「黎民阻饑」不免以命稷，「百姓不親、五品不遜」不免以命契，以是知順成之不可必，猶孝友之不易得也。

translations.literal: Yet even in the ages of Tang and Yu, when "the black-haired people were obstructed by famine" it could not but be entrusted to Ji, and when "the hundred clans were not kindred and the five ranks were not obedient" it could not but be entrusted to Xie — from this one knows that smooth completion cannot be assured, just as filial piety and fraternity are not easily attained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even in the era of Yao and Shun, when "the common people were beset by famine," Yao had no choice but to appoint Ji; when "the people were estranged and the five ranks were in disorder," he had no choice but to appoint Xie. From this we know that a full harvest cannot be guaranteed any more than filial piety and brotherly love can be easily found.

sentences.zh: 是故「有年」、「大有年」以異書于聖人之經，孝友以至行傳于歷代之史，勸農興孝之教不廢於歷代之政，孝弟力田自漢以來有其科。

translations.literal: Therefore "a year of harvest" and "a great year of harvest" are written with distinction in the sage's classics; filial piety and fraternity as supreme conduct are transmitted in the annals of successive dynasties; teachings to encourage agriculture and promote filial piety have not been abandoned in the policies of successive ages; filial sons, brothers, and the vigorous in farming have had their examination category since Han.
translations.idiomatic: Thus "there shall be harvest" and "there shall be great harvest" receive special record in the sage's canonical texts; filial piety and fraternity as the highest conduct are handed down in histories dynasty after dynasty; policies encouraging farming and promoting filial devotion have never ceased across the ages; and since the Han, there has been an official category for filial sons, dutiful brothers, and those who vigorously farmed their fields.

sentences.zh: 章宗嘗曰：「孝義之人，素行已備，雖有希覬，猶不失為行善。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangzong once said: "People of filial righteousness already have their conduct complete; even if they harbor some expectation, they still do not fail to perform good deeds."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangzong once remarked: "Those who embody filial righteousness have already perfected their conduct; even if they harbor some personal hope, they still cannot be said to have failed in doing good."

sentences.zh: 」庶幾帝王之善訓矣。

translations.literal: " — this approaches the good instruction of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: This nearly amounts to the excellent counsel of sage rulers.

sentences.zh: 夫金世孝友見於旌表、載於史冊者僅六人焉。

translations.literal: In the Jin dynasty, those whose filial piety and fraternity were recognized with commendation and recorded in annals numbered only six persons.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin, only six individuals whose filial and fraternal conduct earned public honor and a place in the historical records can be found.

sentences.zh: 作《孝友傳》。

translations.literal: [This account] composes "Biographies of Filial Piety and Fraternity."
translations.idiomatic: A "Biography of Filial Piety and Brotherly Regard" is hereby composed.

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕斡魯補

translations.literal: Wendihan Wolubu
translations.idiomatic: Wendihan Wolubu

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕斡魯補，西北路宋葛斜斯渾猛安人。

translations.literal: Wendihan Wolubu was a native of Hunmeng'an in Songgexisi, Northwestern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihan Wolubu came from Hunmeng'an in Songgexisi on the Northwestern Circuit.

sentences.zh: 年十五，居父喪，不飲酒食肉，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: At age fifteen, while observing mourning for his father, he drank no wine and ate no meat, and built a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen, during his father's mourning period, he abstained from wine and meat and lived in a hut beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 母疾，刲股肉療之，疾愈。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh to treat her, and the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his own thigh to heal her, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 詔以為護衛。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him as a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the Imperial Guard by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 陳顏，衛州汲縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Yan was a native of Ji County in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan was from Ji County in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 世業農。

translations.literal: His family profession was farming for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 父光，宋季擢武舉第，調壽陽尉，未赴。

translations.literal: His father Guang, in the late Song period, was selected in the military examination and was assigned as magistrate of Shouyang, but had not yet taken up the post.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang, in the late Song, passed the military examination and was appointed magistrate of Shouyang, but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 值金兵取汴，光病，圍城中。

translations.literal: When the Jin army captured Bian, Guang fell ill and was trapped inside the besieged city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army captured Bianliang, Guang fell ill and was trapped inside the besieged city.

sentences.zh: 顏間關渡河，往省其父，因扶疾北歸。

translations.literal: Yan made his way with difficulty across the river to visit his father, and thereby escorted the sick man back north.
translations.idiomatic: Yan braved hardship to cross the river and visit his father, then escorted the ailing man back north.

sentences.zh: 光家奴謀良不可，誣告光與賊殺人。

translations.literal: Guang's household slave Mou Liang, unable to carry out his plot, falsely accused Guang of killing people together with bandits.
translations.idiomatic: A household slave named Mou Liang, unable to carry out his scheme, falsely accused Guang of murdering people together with bandits.

sentences.zh: 光系獄，榜掠不勝，因自誣服。

translations.literal: Guang was imprisoned; unable to endure beating under torture, he thus falsely confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was thrown into prison; unable to endure the torture, he falsely confessed to the crime.

sentences.zh: 顏詣郡請代父死，太守徐某哀之，不敢決，適帥臣至郡，以其狀白，帥曰：「此真孝子也。

translations.literal: Yan went to the prefecture to request dying in his father's place; Prefect Xu was moved with pity for him and dared not decide; just then the circuit commander arrived at the prefecture, and [Xu] reported the matter to him; the commander said: "This is a true filial son."
translations.idiomatic: Yan went to the prefectural seat and asked to die in his father's place. Prefect Xu was moved with pity but dared not decide the matter. When the circuit commander happened to arrive, Xu reported the case to him. The commander said, "This is a true filial son."

sentences.zh: 」遂並釋之。

translations.literal: " — and thereupon both were released.
translations.idiomatic: Both father and son were then released.

sentences.zh: 天會七年，詔旌表其門閭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui, an edict commended and marked his household gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianhui, an edict ordered that his household gate be publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 劉瑜，棣州人。

translations.literal: Liu Yu was a native of Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was from Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 家貧甚，母喪不能具葬，乃質其子以給喪事。

translations.literal: His family was extremely poor; at his mother's death he could not provide a full burial, and so pledged his son to fund the funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: His family was desperately poor. When his mother died, he could not afford a proper burial and had to pledge his son as collateral to pay for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，詔賜粟帛，複其終身。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang, an edict bestowed grain and cloth and exempted him for life.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Mingchang, an edict granted him grain and cloth and exempted him from corvée labor for life.

sentences.zh: 孟興，蚤喪父，事母孝謹，母沒，喪葬盡禮。

translations.literal: Meng Xing lost his father early; he served his mother with filial care and respect; when his mother died, the mourning and burial were conducted with full propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xing lost his father at an early age. He served his mother with filial devotion and care. When she died, he conducted the mourning and burial with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 事兄如事其父。

translations.literal: He served his elder brother as he served his father.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his elder brother with the same devotion he would have shown his father.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，詔賜帛十匹、粟二十石。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang, an edict bestowed ten bolts of cloth and twenty piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Mingchang, an edict granted him ten bolts of cloth and twenty piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 王震，甯海州文登縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen was a native of Wendeng County in Ninghaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen was from Wendeng County in Ninghaizhou.

sentences.zh: 為進士學。

translations.literal: He studied for the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 母患風疾，刲股肉雜飲食中，疾遂愈。

translations.literal: When his mother suffered from wind ailment, he cut flesh from his thigh and mixed it in her food and drink, and the illness was thereby cured.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother suffered from a paralytic ailment, he cut flesh from his thigh and mixed it into her food and drink, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 母沒，哀泣過禮，目生翳。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his grieving and weeping exceeded propriety, and cataracts formed in his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his mourning exceeded all propriety in its grief, and cataracts formed in his eyes.

sentences.zh: 服除，目不療而愈，皆以為孝感所致。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, his eyes healed without treatment, and all regarded this as caused by the moving power of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, his eyes healed without any treatment, and everyone attributed this to the power of his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 特賜同進士出身，詔尚書省擬注職任。

translations.literal: He was specially granted jinshi status by imperial favor, and an edict directed the Ministry of Personnel to propose an office assignment.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted jinshi status by imperial favor, and the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to propose an office for him.

sentences.zh: 劉政，洺州人。

translations.literal: Liu Zheng was a native of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng was from Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 性篤孝，母老喪明，政每以舌舐母目，逾旬母能視物。

translations.literal: By nature deeply filial, when his aged mother lost her sight, Zheng each day licked her eyes with his tongue; after more than ten days his mother could see objects.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, when his aged mother went blind, Zheng licked her eyes with his tongue each day. After more than ten days, his mother could see again.

sentences.zh: 母疾，晝夜侍側，衣不解帶，刲股肉啖之者再三。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he attended her day and night at her side, never loosening his belt, and cut flesh from his thigh for her to eat on several occasions.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he attended her day and night without loosening his belt even to sleep, and several times cut flesh from his thigh for her to eat.

sentences.zh: 母死，負土起墳，鄉鄰欲佐其勞，政謝之。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he carried earth to raise the tomb mound; neighbors wished to assist his labor, but Zheng declined.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he carried earth himself to build her tomb. Neighbors offered to help with the labor, but Zheng refused.

sentences.zh: 葬之日，飛鳥哀鳴，翔集丘木間。

translations.literal: On the day of the burial, flying birds cried mournfully and circled to perch among the trees on the mound.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the burial, birds cried mournfully and circled to perch in the trees on the mound.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓側者三年。

translations.literal: He dwelt in a hut beside the tomb for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a hut beside the tomb for three years.

sentences.zh: 防禦使以聞，除太子掌飲丞。

translations.literal: The defense commissioner reported this to the throne, and [Zheng] was appointed Director of Beverages to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The defense commissioner reported his conduct to the throne, and Zheng was appointed Director of Beverages to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 孔子稱逸民伯夷、叔齊、夷逸、硃張、柳下惠、少連，其立心造行之異同，各有所稱謂，而柳下惠則又嘗仕於當世者也。

translations.literal: Confucius praised the reclusive worthies Bo Yi, Shu Qi, Yi Yi, Zhu Zhang, Liuxia Hui, and Shaolian; in the differences and similarities of their established intent and conduct, each had his own designation, yet Liuxia Hui had also once served in his own age.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius praised the reclusive worthies Bo Yi, Shu Qi, Yi Yi, Zhu Zhang, Liuxia Hui, and Shaolian. Though each differed in purpose and conduct and received a distinct epithet, Liuxia Hui had also once held office in his own time.

sentences.zh: 長沮、桀溺之徒，則無所取焉。

translations.literal: As for the likes of Changju and Jieni, he took nothing from them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the likes of Changju and Jieni, he had nothing approving to say of them.

sentences.zh: 後世，凡隱遁之士，其名皆列于史傳，何歟？

translations.literal: In later ages, all reclusive scholars have their names listed in historical biographies — why is this?
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, the names of all reclusive scholars are recorded in historical biographies — why is this?

sentences.zh: 蓋古之仕者，其志將以行道，其為貧而仕下列者，猶必先事而後食焉。

translations.literal: For ancient officeholders, their intent was to practice the Way; even those who took lower posts out of poverty still had to serve first and eat afterward.
translations.idiomatic: For in antiquity, those who took office intended to practice the Way; even those who accepted humble posts out of poverty still put service before salary.

sentences.zh: 後世幹祿者多，其先人尚人之志與歎老嗟卑之心，能去是者鮮矣。

translations.literal: In later ages those who sought emolument were many; the intent of their forebears to esteem others and the heart that sighs at age and laments low station — those who could cast these off were few.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, office-seekers were legion, and few could shed the ambition of their forebears to win favor from superiors, or the habit of lamenting one's age and rank.

sentences.zh: 故君子于士之遠引高蹈者特稱述之，庶聞其風猶足以立懦廉頑也。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman especially commends and recounts scholars who withdraw far and tread high, hoping that hearing their spirit may still suffice to establish the cowardly, make the greedy honest, and stiffen the obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the gentleman especially commends those scholars who withdraw from the world and hold themselves aloof, hoping that even hearing of their spirit may still embolden the timid, shame the greedy, and stiffen the obstinate.

sentences.zh: 作《隱逸傳》。

translations.literal: [This account] composes "Biographies of Reclusion."
translations.idiomatic: A "Biography of Reclusion" is hereby composed.

sentences.zh: 褚承亮

translations.literal: Chu Chengliang
translations.idiomatic: Chu Chengliang

sentences.zh: 褚承亮，字茂先，真定人。

translations.literal: Chu Chengliang, style name Maoxian, was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Chengliang, style name Maoxian, was from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 宋蘇軾自定武謫官過真定，承亮以文謁之，大為稱賞。

translations.literal: When the Song's Su Shi passed through Zhending on his way from demotion at Dingwu, Chengliang presented his writings to him and was greatly praised and admired.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song poet Su Shi passed through Zhending on his way from demotion at Dingwu, Chengliang presented his writings to him and won his high praise.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年秋，應鄉試，同試者八百人，承亮為第一。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Xuanhe, he took the provincial examination; among eight hundred fellow candidates, Chengliang ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year of Xuanhe, he took the provincial examination. Among eight hundred candidates, Chengliang ranked first.

sentences.zh: 明年，登第。

translations.literal: The following year, he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 調易州戶曹，未赴，會金兵南下。

translations.literal: He was assigned as registrar of households in Yizhou but had not yet taken up the post when the Jin army marched south.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as registrar of households in Yizhou but had not yet taken up the post when the Jin army marched south.

sentences.zh: 天會六年，斡離不既破真定，拘籍境內進士試安國寺，承亮名亦在籍中，匿而不出。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui, after Wolibu had captured Zhending, he registered and summoned jinshi within the territory to be examined at Anguo Temple; Chengliang's name was also on the register, but he hid himself and did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhui, after Wolibu captured Zhending, he registered all jinshi degree holders in the region and summoned them to an examination at Anguo Temple. Chengliang's name was on the register, but he hid himself and did not appear.

sentences.zh: 軍中知其才，嚴令押赴，與諸生對策。

translations.literal: The army knew of his talent and issued strict orders to escort him there; he answered policy questions together with the other candidates.
translations.idiomatic: The army knew of his talent and issued strict orders to bring him in. He answered the policy questions together with the other candidates.

sentences.zh: 策問「上皇無道、少帝失信。

translations.literal: The policy question asked: "The Retired Emperor was without the Way and the Young Emperor broke faith."
translations.idiomatic: The policy question asked: "The Retired Emperor was without the Way, and the Young Emperor broke faith."

sentences.zh: 」舉人承風旨，極口詆毀。

translations.literal: " — the candidates followed the intended tone and vilified them to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The candidates followed the intended tone and vilified the Song emperors to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 承亮詣主文劉侍中曰：「君父之罪，豈臣子所得言耶？

translations.literal: Chengliang went to the chief examiner, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu, and said: "The crimes of ruler and father — how can subjects and sons presume to speak of them?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang went to the chief examiner, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu, and said, "The crimes of one's sovereign and father — how can a subject presume to speak of them?"

sentences.zh: 」長揖而出。

translations.literal: " — and with a deep bow he departed.
translations.idiomatic: With a deep bow, he walked out.

sentences.zh: 劉為之動容。

translations.literal: Liu was moved by this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 餘悉放第，凡七十二人，遂號七十二賢榜。

translations.literal: The rest were all passed and given degrees — seventy-two persons in all — and this came to be called the Seventy-Two Worthies list.
translations.idiomatic: All the rest were passed and given degrees — seventy-two in all — and this came to be known as the list of the Seventy-Two Worthies.

sentences.zh: 狀元許必仕為郎官，一日出左掖門，墮馬，首中閫石死，餘皆無顯者。

translations.literal: The top graduate Xu Bishi became a court gentleman; one day as he went out the Left Yabo Gate, he fell from his horse and his head struck the gate stone and he died; the rest achieved no distinction.
translations.idiomatic: The top graduate Xu Bishi became a court gentleman. One day, as he went out the Left Yabo Gate, he fell from his horse; his head struck the gate stone and he died. None of the rest achieved any distinction.

sentences.zh: 劉多承亮之誼，薦知槁城縣。

translations.literal: Liu, greatly impressed by Chengliang's integrity, recommended him as magistrate of Gaocheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, deeply impressed by Chengliang's integrity, recommended him as magistrate of Gaocheng County.

sentences.zh: 漫應之，即棄去。

translations.literal: He casually agreed, then immediately abandoned the post and left.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed perfunctorily, then immediately abandoned the post and left.

sentences.zh: 年七十終，門人私諡曰「玄貞先生。」

translations.literal: He died at age seventy; his disciples privately gave him the posthumous title "Master Xuanzhen."
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy. His disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master Xuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 子席珍，正隆二年進士，官州縣有聲。

translations.literal: His son Xizhen passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenglong and gained renown in prefectural and county offices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xizhen passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenglong and earned a fine reputation in prefectural and county office.

sentences.zh: 王去非

translations.literal: Wang Qufei
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qufei

sentences.zh: 王去非，字廣道，平陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Qufei, style name Guangdao, was a native of Pingyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qufei, style name Guangdao, was from Pingyin.

sentences.zh: 嘗就舉，不得意即屏去，督妻孥耕織以給伏臘。

translations.literal: He once attempted the examinations; when dissatisfied with the outcome he immediately withdrew, and directed his wife and children in farming and weaving to supply the seasonal observances.
translations.idiomatic: He once attempted the examinations. When the results disappointed him, he withdrew at once and had his wife and children farm and weave to supply the household through the seasons.

sentences.zh: 家居教授，束修有餘輒分惠人。

translations.literal: At home he taught students; whenever his tuition fees exceeded his needs he would share them with others.
translations.idiomatic: He taught students at home, and whenever his tuition fees exceeded his needs, he shared the surplus with others.

sentences.zh: 弟子班晄冘貧不能朝夕，一女及笄，去非為辦資裝嫁之。

translations.literal: His student Ban Zhao was extremely poor and could not manage day to day; when a daughter came of age, Qufei provided her dowry and married her off.
translations.idiomatic: His student Ban Zhao was desperately poor and could barely get by. When a daughter came of age, Qufei provided her dowry and saw her married.

sentences.zh: 北鄰有喪忌東出，西與北皆人居，南則去非家，去非壞蠶室使喪南出，遂得葬焉。

translations.literal: A northern neighbor had a funeral and, observing taboo against proceeding east, could not; west and north were both occupied by residences, while south lay Qufei's home; Qufei demolished his silkworm nursery so the funeral procession could go south, and thus burial was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: A northern neighbor needed to conduct a funeral but taboo forbade proceeding east. West and north were both occupied by other homes, while Qufei's house lay to the south. Qufei demolished his silkworm nursery so the funeral procession could go south, and the burial was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 大定二十四年卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-fourth year of Dading, at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fourth year of Dading, at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 趙質，字景道，遼相思溫之裔。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhi, style name Jingdao, was a descendant of the Liao's Sixian Wen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi, style name Jingdao, was a descendant of the Liao's Sixian Wen clan.

sentences.zh: 大定末，舉進士不第，隱居燕城南，教授為業。

translations.literal: In the late Dading period, he took the jinshi examination but did not pass, and retired to live south of Yan's walls, making teaching his profession.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Dading period, he failed the jinshi examination and retired to live south of Yanjing, supporting himself by teaching.

sentences.zh: 明昌間，章宗游春水過焉，聞弦誦聲，幸其齋舍，見壁間所題詩，諷詠久之，賞其志趣不凡。

translations.literal: During the Mingchang era, Emperor Zhangzong, while touring the spring waters, passed by there, heard the sound of recitation, and visited his study; seeing the poems inscribed on the walls, he chanted them for a long while and admired his extraordinary aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mingchang era, Emperor Zhangzong, while touring the spring waters, passed by and heard the sound of students reciting their lessons. He visited Zhi's study, saw the poems inscribed on the walls, and chanted them at length, admiring his extraordinary spirit.

sentences.zh: 召至行殿，命之官。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the traveling palace and ordered to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was summoned to the traveling palace and offered an official post.

sentences.zh: 因辭曰：「臣僻性野逸，志在長林豐草，金鑣玉絡非所願也。

translations.literal: He thereupon declined, saying: "Your subject has a secluded nature and wild ease; his intent lies in deep forests and lush meadows — golden bridles and jade trappings are not what he wishes."
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "Your subject has a reclusive nature and loves the wild. My heart lies among deep forests and lush meadows; golden bridles and jade trappings are not what I desire."

sentences.zh: 況聖明在上，可不容巢、由為外臣乎。

translations.literal: Moreover, with a sage and enlightened ruler above, how could one not allow Chao and You to remain as subjects outside [the court]?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with a sage ruler on the throne, surely Your Majesty can allow men like Chao Fu and Xu You to remain as recluses beyond the court?

sentences.zh: 」上益奇之，賜田畝千，複之終身。

translations.literal: " — the emperor was all the more struck by him and bestowed a thousand mu of fields, exempting him for life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was all the more impressed and granted him a thousand mu of fields, exempting him from corvée labor for life.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Taihe, at age eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Taihe, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 杜時升

translations.literal: Du Shisheng
translations.idiomatic: Du Shisheng

sentences.zh: 杜時升，字進之，霸州信安人。

translations.literal: Du Shisheng, style name Jinzhi, was a native of Xin'an in Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shisheng, style name Jinzhi, was from Xin'an in Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 博學知天文，不肯仕進。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and versed in astronomy, he refused to pursue office.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and versed in astronomy, he refused to pursue office.

sentences.zh: 承安、泰和間，宰相數薦時升可大用。

translations.literal: During the Cheng'an and Taihe periods, the chief ministers repeatedly recommended that Shisheng could be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Cheng'an and Taihe periods, the chief ministers repeatedly recommended him for high office.

sentences.zh: 時升謂所親曰：「吾觀正北赤氣如血，東西亙天，天下當大亂，亂而南北當合為一。

translations.literal: Shisheng said to those close to him: "I observe crimson vapor like blood in the due north, stretching east and west across the sky; the realm will suffer great disorder, and after the disorder north and south will become one."
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng told those close to him, "I see crimson vapor like blood in the north, stretching east and west across the sky. The realm will fall into great disorder, and when the turmoil ends, north and south will become one."

sentences.zh: 消息盈虛，迴圈無端，察往考來，孰能違之。

translations.literal: Growth and decline, fullness and emptiness, cycle without end — examining the past and investigating what is to come, who can defy this?
translations.idiomatic: Growth and decline, fullness and emptiness — the cycle has no end. When one examines the past and considers what is to come, who can defy it?

sentences.zh: 」是時，風俗侈靡，紀綱大壞，世宗之業遂衰。

translations.literal: " — at this time customs were extravagant and dissolute, regulations were greatly broken down, and the enterprise of Emperor Shizong thus declined.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, customs had grown extravagant, institutions were breaking down, and the achievements of Emperor Shizong were fading.

sentences.zh: 時升乃南渡河，隱居嵩、洛山中，從學者甚眾。

translations.literal: Shisheng then crossed the river southward and retired to the Song and Luo mountains, where those who came to study under him were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng then crossed the river south and retired to the Song and Luo mountains, where he attracted a great many students.

sentences.zh: 大抵以「伊洛之學」教人自時升始。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, teaching people the "learning of Yi and Luo" began with Shisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, the teaching of Neo-Confucian learning to students in this region began with Shisheng.

sentences.zh: 正大間，大元兵攻潼關，拒守甚堅，眾皆相賀，時升曰：「大兵皆在秦、鞏間，若假道于宋，出襄、漢入宛、葉，鐵騎長驅勢如風雨，無高山大川為之阻，土崩之勢也。

translations.literal: During the Zhengda period, the Great Yuan army attacked Tong Pass and the defense was very firm; the multitude all congratulated one another; Shisheng said: "The great army is all between Qin and Gong; if they borrow passage through Song, emerge from Xiang and Han into Wan and Ye, iron cavalry will drive straight through like wind and rain — with no high mountains or great rivers to obstruct them, it will be a landslide collapse."
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengda period, the Great Yuan army attacked Tong Pass, and the defense held firm. Everyone congratulated one another, but Shisheng said, "The main force is all between Qin and Gong. If they borrow passage through Song territory, emerge from Xiang and Han into Wan and Ye, and drive their iron cavalry straight through like wind and rain, with no high mountains or great rivers to obstruct them, the Jin will collapse like a landslide."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，大元兵果自饒峰關涉襄陽出南陽，金人敗績於三峰山，汴京不守，皆如時升所料雲。

translations.literal: " — before long, the Great Yuan army indeed crossed Raofeng Pass through Xiangyang and emerged at Nanyang; the Jin suffered defeat at Sanfeng Mountain; Bian was not held — all came to pass as Shisheng had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the Great Yuan army did indeed cross Raofeng Pass through Xiangyang and emerge at Nanyang. The Jin suffered defeat at Sanfeng Mountain, and Bianjing fell — all exactly as Shisheng had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 正大末，卒。

translations.literal: In the late Zhengda period, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the late Zhengda period.

sentences.zh: 郝天挺

translations.literal: Hao Tianting
translations.idiomatic: Hao Tianting

sentences.zh: 郝天挺，字晉卿，澤州陵川人。

translations.literal: Hao Tianting, style name Jinqing, was a native of Lingchuan in Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Tianting, style name Jinqing, was from Lingchuan in Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 早衰多疾，厭於科舉，遂不復充賦。

translations.literal: He declined early and suffered many illnesses, grew weary of the civil examinations, and therefore never again submitted his examination composition.
translations.idiomatic: He declined early and was often ill. Weary of the civil examinations, he never again submitted his examination composition.

sentences.zh: 太原元好問嘗從學進士業，天挺曰：「今人賦學以速售為功，六經百家分磔緝綴，或篇章句讀不之知，幸而得之，不免為庸人。

translations.literal: Yuan Haowen of Taiyuan once studied for the jinshi degree under him. Tianting said: "People today study examination essays with quick sale as their achievement; the Six Classics and the hundred schools are dismembered and pieced together — some do not even know chapters, passages, or how to parse sentences; if by luck they obtain [a degree], they cannot avoid being mediocre men."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Haowen of Taiyuan once studied for the jinshi under him. Tianting said, "Students today treat examination essays as a trade for quick success. They chop up the Six Classics and the hundred schools and stitch the pieces together — some cannot even parse a chapter or a sentence. If they luck into a degree, they are still mediocre."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「讀書不為藝文，選官不為利養，唯通人能之。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Reading books not for literary craft, taking office not for profit and sustenance — only the thoroughly accomplished can do this."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Reading not for literary display, taking office not for profit — only a truly accomplished man can do that."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「今之仕多以貪敗，皆苦饑寒不能自持耳。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Those who take office today mostly fail through greed — all because they cannot endure hunger and cold and cannot hold themselves steady."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Officials today mostly ruin themselves through greed because they cannot endure hunger and cold."

sentences.zh: 丈夫不耐饑寒，一事不可為。

translations.literal: A man who cannot endure hunger and cold cannot accomplish a single thing.
translations.idiomatic: A man who cannot endure hunger and cold cannot accomplish anything worthwhile.

sentences.zh: 子以吾言求之，科舉在其中矣。

translations.literal: You, sir, seek it through my words — the civil examinations lie within them.
translations.idiomatic: Seek what you need through my teaching, and the examinations are already within it.

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「以此學進士無乃戾乎？

translations.literal: " Someone said: "To study this way for the jinshi — is that not contrary?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Studying this way for the jinshi — is that not contrary to the examination?"

sentences.zh: 」天挺曰：「正欲渠不為舉子爾。

translations.literal: " Tianting said: "I precisely want you not to become an examination candidate."
translations.idiomatic: Tianting said, "I precisely want you not to become a mere examination candidate."

sentences.zh: 」貞祐中，居河南，往來淇衛間。

translations.literal: " During the Zhenyou period he lived in Henan, traveling back and forth between Qi and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyou period he lived in Henan, traveling between Qi and Wei.

sentences.zh: 為人有崖岸，耿耿自信，寧落魄困窮，終不一至豪富之門。

translations.literal: In conduct he had steep banks and edges, upright and self-confident; he would rather be down and out in poverty than once visit the gates of the wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: He had a steep, unyielding character and trusted himself completely. He would rather remain poor and destitute than once visit a wealthy man's gate.

sentences.zh: 年五十，終於舞陽。

translations.literal: At age fifty, he died at Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Wuyang at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 薛繼元

translations.literal: Xue Jiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jiyuan

sentences.zh: 薛繼先，字曼卿。

translations.literal: Xue Jixian, style name Manqing.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jixian, style name Manqing.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，隱居洛西山中，課童子讀書。

translations.literal: After the southward migration, he retired to live in the western mountains of Luo and taught boys to read.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward migration, he retired to the western mountains of Luoyang and taught boys to read.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，與人交謙遜和雅，所居化之。

translations.literal: He served his mother with filial piety; in dealings with others he was modest, yielding, and refined, and those among whom he lived were transformed by him.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother filially. In dealings with others he was modest and refined, and those around him were transformed by his example.

sentences.zh: 子純孝，字方叔，有父風。

translations.literal: His son Chunxiao, style name Fangshu, had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chunxiao, style name Fangshu, had his father's character.

sentences.zh: 有詐為曼卿書就方叔取物者，曼卿年已老狀貌如少者，客不知其為曼卿而以為方叔也，而與之書，曼卿如所取付之。

translations.literal: Someone once forged a letter in Manqing's name and went to Fangshu to obtain goods. Manqing was already old but his appearance was like a younger man's; the visitor did not know he was Manqing and thought he was Fangshu, and gave him the letter — Manqing paid out what was requested as written.
translations.idiomatic: Someone forged a letter in Manqing's name and went to Fangshu to obtain goods. Manqing was old but still looked young; the visitor mistook him for Fangshu and handed him the letter. Manqing paid out what was requested without question.

sentences.zh: 監察禦史石玠行部過曼卿，曼卿不之見。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Shi Jie, while on an inspection tour, passed Manqing's place; Manqing did not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Shi Jie passed through on an inspection tour, but Manqing refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 或言：「君何無鄉曲情。

translations.literal: Someone said: "Sir, why show no regard for your fellow townsman?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Why show no regard for a fellow townsman?"

sentences.zh: 」曼卿曰：「君未之思耳。

translations.literal: Manqing said: "You have not thought it through."
translations.idiomatic: Manqing said, "You have not thought it through."

sentences.zh: 凡今時政未必皆善，禦史一有所劾，將謂自我發之。

translations.literal: "All policies of the present day are not necessarily good. If the censor impeaches something, people will say it began with me.
translations.idiomatic: All policies of the day are not necessarily good. If the censor impeaches something, people will say I set it in motion.

sentences.zh: 同惡相庇，他日並鄉里必有受禍者。

translations.literal: Those who shield one another in shared wrongdoing — someday people of our hometown will surely suffer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who shield one another in shared wrongdoing — someday our neighbors will suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 」其畏慎皆此類。

translations.literal: " His caution in such matters was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His caution was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 壬辰之亂，病沒宜陽。

translations.literal: In the disorder of the renchen year, he died of illness at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the disorder of the renchen year, he died of illness at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 高仲振

translations.literal: Gao Zhongzhen
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhongzhen

sentences.zh: 高仲振，字正之，遼東人。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongzhen, style name Zhengzhi, was a native of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhongzhen, style name Zhengzhi, was from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 其兄領開封鎮兵，仲振依之以居。

translations.literal: His elder brother commanded the garrison troops at Kaifeng, and Zhongzhen lived with him in dependence.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother commanded the Kaifeng garrison, and Zhongzhen lived with him.

sentences.zh: 既而以家業付其兄，挈妻子入嵩山。

translations.literal: Thereafter he entrusted the family estate to his brother, took wife and children, and entered Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He then entrusted the family estate to his brother, took his wife and children, and retired to Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 博極群書，尤深《易》《皇極經世》學。

translations.literal: He read exhaustively among all books, especially penetrating the learning of the Changes and the Huangji Jingshi.
translations.idiomatic: He read exhaustively among all books, especially mastering the Changes and the Huangji Jingshi.

sentences.zh: 安貧自樂，不入城市，山野小人亦知敬之。

translations.literal: Content with poverty and delighting in his lot, he did not enter cities; even rustic fellows of mountain and wild knew to respect him.
translations.idiomatic: Content with poverty and delighting in his lot, he never entered the cities. Even mountain rustics knew to respect him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與其弟子張潛、王汝梅行山谷間，人望之翩然如仙。

translations.literal: He once walked through mountain valleys with his disciples Zhang Qian and Wang Rumei; people who saw them from afar thought them like immortals drifting along.
translations.idiomatic: He once walked through mountain valleys with his disciples Zhang Qian and Wang Rumei. People who glimpsed them from afar thought them like immortals drifting along.

sentences.zh: 或曰仲振嘗遇異人教以養生術，嘗終日燕坐，骨節戛戛有聲，所談皆世外事，有扣之者輒不復語雲。

translations.literal: Some say Zhongzhen once met an extraordinary man who taught him the art of nurturing life; he could sit all day in repose, his joints crackling audibly; what he discussed were all matters beyond the world — if questioned he would speak no more, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Zhongzhen once met an extraordinary man who taught him the art of nurturing life. He could sit in repose all day, his joints crackling audibly. What he discussed were matters beyond this world; if pressed, he would say no more.

sentences.zh: 張潛，字仲升，武清人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qian, style name Zhongsheng, was a native of Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian, style name Zhongsheng, was from Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 幼有志節，慕荊軻、聶政為人，年三十始折節讀書。

translations.literal: In youth he had high resolve and admired the conduct of Jing Ke and Nie Zheng; only at age thirty did he restrain himself and take up reading.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he aspired to heroic resolve and admired Jing Ke and Nie Zheng. Only at thirty did he restrain himself and take up reading.

sentences.zh: 時人高其行誼，目曰「張古人。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his conduct and called him "Zhang the Ancient."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time admired his conduct and called him "Zhang the Ancient."

sentences.zh: 」後客崧山，從仲振受《易》。

translations.literal: " Later he lodged at Mount Song and received instruction in the Changes from Zhongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Later he lodged at Mount Song and studied the Changes under Zhongzhen.

sentences.zh: 年五十，始娶魯山孫氏，亦有賢行，夫婦相敬如賓，負薪拾穗，行歌自得，不知其貧也。

translations.literal: At age fifty he first married into the Sun clan of Lushan; she too had worthy conduct; husband and wife respected each other as guests, carried firewood and gathered fallen grain, walked singing contentedly, unaware of their poverty.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty he first married a woman of the Sun clan of Lushan, who was likewise virtuous. Husband and wife respected each other as guests, carried firewood and gathered fallen grain, and walked along singing — unaware of their poverty.

sentences.zh: 鄰里有為潛種瓜者，及熟讓潛，潛弗許，竟分而食之。

translations.literal: A neighbor once planted melons for Qian; when they ripened he offered them to Qian, but Qian would not accept and in the end they divided and ate them together.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor once planted melons for Qian. When they ripened he offered them to Qian, who refused; in the end they divided and ate them together.

sentences.zh: 嘗行道中拾一斧，夫婦計度移時，乃持歸訪其主還之。

translations.literal: Once on the road they picked up an axe; husband and wife deliberated for some time, then took it home and sought out its owner to return it.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road they picked up an axe. Husband and wife deliberated for some time, then took it home, found its owner, and returned it.

sentences.zh: 裏有兄弟分財者，其弟曰：「我家如此，獨不畏張先生知耶？

translations.literal: In the village were brothers dividing family property; the younger said: "Our household is like this — are we not afraid Zhang the Gentleman will know?"
translations.idiomatic: In the village, brothers were dividing family property. The younger said, "Our household is like this — are we not afraid Mr. Zhang will find out?"

sentences.zh: 」遂如初。

translations.literal: " And they reverted to the original arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: They reverted to the original arrangement.

sentences.zh: 天興間，潛挈家避兵少室，乃不食七日死，孫氏亦投絕澗死焉。

translations.literal: During the Tianxing period, Qian led his family to escape warfare at Shaoshi; he then fasted for seven days and died; Lady Sun also threw herself into a deep ravine and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxing period, Qian led his family to Shaoshi to escape warfare. He fasted for seven days and died; Lady Sun also threw herself into a deep ravine and died.

sentences.zh: 王汝梅

translations.literal: Wang Rumei
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rumei

sentences.zh: 王汝梅，字大用，大名人。

translations.literal: Wang Rumei, style name Dayong, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rumei, style name Dayong, was from Daming.

sentences.zh: 始由律學為伊陽簿，秩滿，遂隱居不仕。

translations.literal: He first entered office through legal studies as registrar of Yiyang; when his term ended, he retired and never took office again.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered office through legal studies as registrar of Yiyang. When his term ended, he retired and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 性嗜書，動有禮法。

translations.literal: By nature he loved books and in all his movements observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books by nature and observed ritual propriety in all his movements.

sentences.zh: 生徒以法經就學者，兼授以經學。

translations.literal: Students who came to study the law canon with him he also instructed in classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Students who came to study the law canon with him he also instructed in the classical learning.

sentences.zh: 諸生服其教，無敢為非義者。

translations.literal: The students submitted to his teaching and none dared do what was not righteous.
translations.idiomatic: His students submitted to his teaching, and none dared do what was not righteous.

sentences.zh: 同業嘗憫其貧，時周之，皆謝不受。

translations.literal: Colleagues once pitied his poverty and from time to time gave him gifts, but he always declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues pitied his poverty and from time to time gave him gifts, but he always declined.

sentences.zh: 後不知所終。

translations.literal: Later no one knew how he ended.
translations.idiomatic: Later no one knew his end.

sentences.zh: 宋可，字予之，武陟人。

translations.literal: Song Ke, style name Yuzhi, was a native of Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ke, style name Yuzhi, was from Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 其姑適大族槁氏，貞祐之兵，夫及子皆死於難。

translations.literal: His paternal aunt had married into the Gao clan, a great family; during the warfare of Zhenyou, her husband and son all died in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal aunt had married into the great Gao clan. During the warfare of Zhenyou, her husband and son all died in the calamity.

sentences.zh: 姑以白金五十笏遺可，可受不辭。

translations.literal: The aunt left Ke fifty ingots of white gold as a bequest; Ke accepted without declining.
translations.idiomatic: The aunt left Ke fifty ingots of white gold. Ke accepted without declining.

sentences.zh: 其後姑得槁氏疏族立為後，挈之省外家。

translations.literal: Later the aunt obtained a distant member of the Gao clan to establish as heir and took him to live outside her maiden family's home.
translations.idiomatic: Later the aunt obtained a distant Gao clansman to establish as heir and took him to live outside her maiden family's home.

sentences.zh: 可乃置酒會鄉鄰，謂姑曰：「姑往時遺可以金，可以槁氏無子故受之。

translations.literal: Ke then set out wine and gathered the neighbors, saying to his aunt: "Aunt, when you formerly left this gold with me, I accepted it because the Gao clan had no son.
translations.idiomatic: Ke then set out wine and gathered the neighbors, telling his aunt, "When you left this gold with me, I accepted because the Gao clan had no heir.

sentences.zh: 今有子矣，此金槁氏物，非姑物也，可何名取之。

translations.literal: Now there is a son; this gold is the Gao clan's property, not the aunt's property — by what name should Ke take it?
translations.idiomatic: Now there is an heir. This gold belongs to the Gao clan, not to you — by what right should I keep it?

sentences.zh: 」因呼妻子舁金歸之，鄉里用是重之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon called wife and children to carry the gold back; the neighborhood thereby held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He called his wife and children to carry the gold back. The neighborhood held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 未幾，北兵駐山陽，軍中有聞可名者，訪知所在，質其子，使人招之曰：「從我者禍福共之，不然，汝子死矣。

translations.literal: Before long, northern troops were stationed at Shanyang; in the army someone who had heard Ke's name inquired where he was, seized his son as hostage, and sent a man to summon him, saying: "Follow me and we shall share fortune and misfortune; otherwise your son dies."
translations.idiomatic: Before long, northern troops were stationed at Shanyang. Someone in the army who had heard Ke's name found where he lived, seized his son as a hostage, and sent a messenger saying, "Follow me and we shall share fortune and misfortune — otherwise your son dies."

sentences.zh: 」親舊競勸之往，可皆謝不從，曰：「吾有子無子，與吾兒死生，皆有命焉。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends all urged him to go; Ke declined them all, saying: "Whether I have a son or not, my son's life and death, like my own, are all a matter of fate.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends urged him to go. Ke declined them all, saying, "Whether I have a son or not, my son's life and death, like my own, are matters of fate.

sentences.zh: 豈以一子故，並平生所守者亡之。

translations.literal: How could I, for the sake of one son, together cast away what I have upheld all my life?
translations.idiomatic: How could I, for one son, cast away what I have upheld all my life?

sentences.zh: 」後竟以無子。

translations.literal: " In the end he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he had no son.

sentences.zh: 辛願，字敬之，福昌人。

translations.literal: Xin Yuan, style name Jingzhi, was a native of Fuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yuan, style name Jingzhi, was from Fuchang.

sentences.zh: 年二十五始知讀書，取《白氏諷諫集》自試，一日便能背誦。

translations.literal: At age twenty-five he first learned to read; he took Bai Juyi's Collection of Admonitions and tested himself — in one day he could recite it from memory.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-five he first learned to read. He took Bai Juyi's Collection of Admonitions and tested himself — in one day he could recite it from memory.

sentences.zh: 乃聚書環堵中讀之，至《書伊訓》、《詩河廣》頗若有所省，欲罷不能，因更致力焉。

translations.literal: He then gathered books and read within walls on all sides; when he reached the Instructions of Yi in the Documents and the Broad River in the Odes he seemed somewhat awakened, wished to stop but could not, and therefore applied himself all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered books and read within his walled room. When he reached the Instructions of Yi in the Documents and the Broad River in the Odes, he seemed somewhat awakened, wished to stop but could not, and applied himself all the more.

sentences.zh: 由是博極書史，作文有繩尺，詩律精嚴有自得之趣。

translations.literal: From this he read exhaustively in books and histories; his essays had measure and rule, and his regulated verse was rigorous with a personal flavor.
translations.idiomatic: From this he read exhaustively in books and histories. His essays had measure and rule; his regulated verse was rigorous with a personal flavor.

sentences.zh: 性野逸，不修威儀，貴人延客，麻衣草屨、足脛赤露坦然於其間，劇談豪飲，傍若無人。

translations.literal: By nature wild and at ease, he did not cultivate imposing bearing; when nobles extended invitations, in hemp robe, straw sandals, and bare shins he sat openly among them, talking freely and drinking boldly as though no one were present.
translations.idiomatic: Wild and at ease by nature, he did not cultivate imposing bearing. When nobles invited him, he sat among them in hemp robe, straw sandals, and bare shins, talking freely and drinking boldly as though no one were present.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂王鬱曰：「王侯將相，世所共嗜者，聖人有以得之亦不避。

translations.literal: He once said to Wang Yu: "Kings, marquises, generals, and ministers — what the age jointly craves — if the sage obtains them he does not avoid them either.
translations.idiomatic: He once said to Wang Yu, "Kings, marquises, generals, and ministers — what the age jointly craves — if the sage obtains them he does not avoid them.

sentences.zh: 得之不以道，與夫居之不能行己之志，是欲澡其身而伏於廁也。

translations.literal: To obtain them not by the Way, or to dwell in them yet unable to carry out one's own intent — that is wanting to bathe the body yet crouching in a privy.
translations.idiomatic: To obtain them not by the Way, or to dwell in them yet be unable to carry out one's own intent — that is wanting to bathe yet crouching in a privy.

sentences.zh: 是難與他人道，子宜保之。

translations.literal: This is hard to speak of to others — you, sir, should keep it to yourself.
translations.idiomatic: This is hard to speak of to others — you should keep it to yourself.

sentences.zh: 」其志趣如此。

translations.literal: " His aspirations were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His aspirations were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 後為河南府治中高廷玉客。

translations.literal: Later he became a retainer of Gao Tingyu, administrative supervisor of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became a retainer of Gao Tingyu, administrative supervisor of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 廷玉為府尹溫蒂罕福興所誣，願亦被訊掠，幾不得免，自是生事益狼狽。

translations.literal: Tingyu was framed by the prefect Wendihan Fuxing; Yuan was also interrogated under torture and nearly could not escape; from this his affairs grew ever more disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu was framed by the prefect Wendihan Fuxing. Yuan was also interrogated under torture and nearly could not escape. From this his affairs grew ever more disordered.

sentences.zh: 願雅負高氣，不以從俗俯仰，迫以饑凍流離，往往見之於詩。

translations.literal: Yuan was by nature proud of high spirit and would not bow to vulgar custom; pressed by hunger, cold, and wandering exile, this often appeared in his poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was proud by nature and would not bow to vulgar custom. Pressed by hunger, cold, and wandering exile, this often appeared in his poetry.

sentences.zh: 有詩數千首，常貯竹橐中。

translations.literal: He had several thousand poems, which he always stored in a bamboo bag.
translations.idiomatic: He had several thousand poems, which he always stored in a bamboo bag.

sentences.zh: 正大末，歿洛下。

translations.literal: In the late Zhengda period, he died at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Zhengda period, he died at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 其詩有雲：「黃綺暫來為漢友，巢由終不是唐臣。

translations.literal: Among his poems is the line: "Huang and Qi came for a time as friends of Han; Chao and You in the end were not ministers of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: Among his poems is the line: "Huang and Qi came for a time as friends of Han; Chao and You in the end were not ministers of Tang."

sentences.zh: 」真處士語也。

translations.literal: " — truly the words of a true recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the words of a true recluse.

sentences.zh: 王予可

translations.literal: Wang Yuke
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuke

sentences.zh: 王予可，字南雲，河東吉州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuke, style name Nanyun, was a native of Jizhou in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuke, style name Nanyun, was from Jizhou in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父本軍校，予可亦嘗隸籍。

translations.literal: His father was originally a military school officer; Yuke also once was enrolled in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: His father was originally a military school officer; Yuke was also once enrolled in the military registers.

sentences.zh: 年三十許，大病後忽發狂，久之能把筆作詩文，及說世外恍惚事。

translations.literal: At about age thirty, after a great illness he suddenly went mad; after a long while he could take up the brush and compose poetry and prose, and speak of vague affairs beyond the world.
translations.idiomatic: At about thirty, after a grave illness he suddenly went mad. After a long while he could take up the brush and compose poetry and prose, and speak of vague affairs beyond this world.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，居上蔡、遂平、郾城之間，遇文士則稱「大成將軍」，于佛前則稱「諦摩龍什」，於道則稱「騶天玄俊」，于貴遊則稱「威錦堂主人」。

translations.literal: After the southward migration he lived among Shangcai, Suiping, and Yancheng; when he met literary gentlemen he called himself "Great Accomplishment General," before the Buddha "Dharma Dragon Shiq," on the Way "Zou Tian Xuanjun," and among noble travelers "Master of the Weijin Hall."
translations.idiomatic: After the southward migration he lived among Shangcai, Suiping, and Yancheng. Before literary gentlemen he called himself Great Accomplishment General; before the Buddha, Dharma Dragon Shiq; on the Way, Zou Tian Xuanjun; among noble travelers, Master of the Weijin Hall.

sentences.zh: 為人軀幹雄偉，貌奇古，戴青葛巾，項後垂雙帶若牛耳，一金鏤環在頂額之間，兩頰以青涅之為翠靨。

translations.literal: In person he was tall and imposing, his appearance strangely ancient; he wore a green ge cloth turban, with twin bands hanging behind his neck like ox ears and a gold-inlaid ring between his brows; on both cheeks he had indigo painted as kingfisher dimples.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and imposing in person, his appearance was strangely ancient. He wore a green ge-cloth turban, with twin bands hanging behind his neck like ox ears and a gold-inlaid ring on his brow; on both cheeks indigo was painted as kingfisher dimples.

sentences.zh: 衣長不能掩脛。

translations.literal: His robes were long yet could not cover his shins.
translations.idiomatic: His robes were long yet could not cover his shins.

sentences.zh: 落魄嗜酒，每入城，市人爭以酒食遺之。

translations.literal: Down and out and addicted to wine, whenever he entered the city the townspeople vied to give him wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: Down and out and addicted to wine, whenever he entered the city the townspeople vied to give him wine and food.

sentences.zh: 夜宿土室中，夏月或屍穢在傍、蛆蟲狼籍不恤也。

translations.literal: At night he slept in earthen rooms; in summer sometimes corpses lay rotting beside him and maggots were scattered in profusion — he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: At night he slept in earthen rooms. In summer corpses sometimes lay rotting beside him and maggots were scattered about — he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 人與之紙，落筆數百言，或詩或文，散漫碎雜，無句讀、無首尾，多六經中語及韻學家古文奇字，字畫峭勁，遇宋諱亦時避之。

translations.literal: When people gave him paper, his brush would produce several hundred words — poetry or prose, scattered and fragmentary, without punctuation or beginning or end, mostly phrases from the Six Classics and archaic odd characters of phonologists; the brushwork was steep and forceful; when he encountered Song taboo names he sometimes avoided them as well.
translations.idiomatic: When given paper, his brush produced several hundred words — poetry or prose, scattered and fragmentary, without punctuation or beginning or end, mostly phrases from the Six Classics and archaic odd characters of phonologists. The brushwork was steep and forceful; he sometimes avoided Song taboo names as well.

sentences.zh: 或問以故事，其應如響，諸所引書，皆世所未見。

translations.literal: If asked about historical matters, his responses were like an echo; all books he cited were unseen in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about historical matters, his responses were like an echo. All books he cited were unseen in the world.

sentences.zh: 談說之際稍若有條貫，則又以誕幻語亂之。

translations.literal: In the midst of discourse he would seem for a moment to have coherence, then confuse it again with fantastic and illusory words.
translations.idiomatic: In discourse he would seem for a moment coherent, then confuse it again with fantastic words.

sentences.zh: 麻九疇、張玨與之遊最狎，言其詩以百分為率，可曉者才二三耳。

translations.literal: Ma Jiuchou and Zhang Jue associated with him most intimately, saying that of his poetry, reckoned by percentage, only two or three parts in ten could be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jiuchou and Zhang Jue associated with him most intimately, saying that of his poetry, by percentage, only two or three parts in ten could be understood.

sentences.zh: 壬辰兵亂，為順天將領所得，知其名，竊議欲挈之北歸，館於州之瑞雲觀。

translations.literal: In the warfare of the renchen year he was taken by a Shuntian commander; knowing his name, they privately discussed taking him north and lodged him at the Ruixun Abbey of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the warfare of the renchen year he was taken by a Shuntian commander. Knowing his name, they privately discussed taking him north and lodged him at the prefecture's Ruixun Abbey.

sentences.zh: 予可明日見將領自言曰：「我不能住君家瑞雲觀也。

translations.literal: The next day Yuke went to see the commander and said of himself: "I cannot stay at your household's Ruixun Abbey."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yuke went to see the commander and said, "I cannot stay at your household's Ruixun Abbey."

sentences.zh: 」不數日卒。

translations.literal: " Within a few days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days he died.

sentences.zh: 後複有見於淮上者。

translations.literal: Later someone again saw him on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone again saw him on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金世隱逸不多見，今于簡冊所有，得十有二人焉。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Recluses of the Jin age are not often seen; those now in the brief records amount to twelve persons.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Recluses of the Jin age are not often seen; those recorded in these annals amount to twelve persons.

sentences.zh: 其卓爾不群者三人。

translations.literal: Among them, three stood out from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, three stood out from the crowd.

sentences.zh: 褚承亮宋人，勒試進士，主司發策問宋徽、欽之罪，承亮長揖而去之。

translations.literal: Chu Chengliang was a Song man; compelled to take the jinshi examination, when the chief examiner issued a policy question on the crimes of Song Huizong and Qinzong, Chengliang made a deep bow and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Chengliang was a Song subject. Compelled to take the jinshi examination, when the chief examiner issued a policy question on the crimes of Huizong and Qinzong of Song, Chengliang made a deep bow and departed.

sentences.zh: 方金人重舉業，杜時升居山中，首以「伊洛之學」教後進。

translations.literal: Just when the Jin people valued the examination curriculum, Du Shisheng lived in the mountains and was the first to teach the younger generation the "learning of Yi and Luo."
translations.idiomatic: Just when the Jin prized the examination curriculum, Du Shisheng lived in the mountains and was the first to teach the younger generation Neo-Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 宋可不願仕，人執其子為質，寧棄而不就，遂以無子。

translations.literal: Song Ke did not wish to take office; men seized his son as hostage; he would rather abandon him than comply, and thus ended without a son.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ke refused office. When men seized his son as a hostage, he would rather abandon the boy than submit, and thus ended without a son.

sentences.zh: 雖制行過中，豈不賢于殺妻以求大將者乎。

translations.literal: Though his conduct exceeded the mean, is he not more worthy than one who kills his wife to seek a great generalship?
translations.idiomatic: Though his conduct exceeded the mean, is he not more worthy than one who killed his wife to win a general's command?

sentences.zh: 大夫士見善明、用心剛，故能為人所難為者如此。

translations.literal: When great officers and scholars see what is good clearly and apply their minds firmly, they can therefore do what others find hard to do — as in cases such as these.
translations.idiomatic: When great officers and scholars see what is good with clarity and set their minds firmly, they can do what others find hard to do — as in cases such as these.
